title: Knee arthroscopy
what: Surgery through 2 or 3 tiny cuts. The surgeon puts a thin camera and tools into the knee and looks at the joint from the inside.
why: For meniscus and ligament injuries, long-term knee pain, or a knee that locks, when other treatment has not helped.
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you ever had blood clots in your veins
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia
Cuts, a rash, or inflammation on the skin of the knee

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a check by a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Usually spinal anesthesia is used, an injection in the back so your legs feel no pain, or general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist chooses together with you.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not shave your knee yourself. Tiny cuts raise the risk of infection. If needed, the clinic will do it.

prepare.title: Things to have
prepare.text: Loose shorts or sweatpants, comfortable shoes, and crutches if the doctor tells you to buy them.

bring: Your knee MRI and X-ray images
A compression stocking, if the doctor prescribed one
steps: You get anesthesia: spinal or general
Your leg is cleaned and covered with sterile sheets
The surgeon makes 2 or 3 cuts, each about one centimeter
A camera and tools go in through the cuts, and the joint is shown on a screen
The surgeon treats what is found, for example the meniscus
The cuts are closed and a bandage is put on
feel: There is no pain during surgery
Afterwards, swelling and pain in the knee. Painkillers help
After spinal anesthesia, your legs are numb for a few hours
after: You often go home the same day or the next day
Sometimes you walk with crutches for a few days. The surgeon will tell you
Cold, keeping the leg raised, and exercises as your doctor advises reduce swelling
Stitches are removed in about 10 to 14 days, unless they dissolve
red_flags: Fever above 38 degrees, pus, or strong redness at the cuts
The knee swells up fast, and the pain gets worse
Swelling and pain in the calf
Shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services right away

faq.q: How soon can I walk after knee arthroscopy?
faq.a: Often you can walk the same day or the next day. The surgeon decides about putting weight on the leg and crutches. It depends on what was done.

faq.q: Do I need general anesthesia for arthroscopy?
faq.a: Not always. Often spinal anesthesia is used: you are awake, but your legs feel no pain.

faq.q: How long is recovery after arthroscopy?
faq.a: Usually from a few weeks to a few months. Physical therapy exercises on your doctor's plan speed up recovery.

reminders.text: Arthroscopy tomorrow. Pack your ID, images, and things. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
